newsitem.title: MALDIVES: S.Asian leaders criticise new Israeli settlements.
newsitem.headline: S.Asian leaders criticise new Israeli settlements.

text.p: South Asian leaders on Wednesday accused Israel of setting back the Mideast peace process and called for the establishment of a sovereign Palestinian state.
Leaders of the seven-nation South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) condemned Israel in a joint declaration at the end of a three-day summit in the Maldives.

The statement said the leaders "expressed concern at the setback to the peace process and unleashing of violence against Palestinian people in occupied territories and the resulting threat to the peace process due to policies of the government of Israel in establishing and enlarging Jewish settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories".
It said the leaders were convinced that the peace process should be continued by honouring previous commitments made by all parties.

"They also called for the restoration of the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people, including the right to self-determination and the establishment of a sovereign state under the leadership of the PLO (Palestine Liberation Organisation), their sole legitimate representative, which could co-exist with its neighbours in peace and harmony," it said.

Palestinians are demanding a halt to Jewish settlement building in East Jerusalem, the rest of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, areas where they envisage an independent state. Israel wants Palestinians to crack down on militants opposed to peace.

PLO officials have criticised Washington for what they said is its refusal to press Israel to halt settlement activities in Palestinian areas during mediation to restart peace talks. Israel says it will not stop building the settlements.
SAARC is comprised of Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
